source.title: History of the Peloponnesian War
source.description:
Thucydides' book is now entitled History of the Peloponnesian War. His entire contribution to history & historiography is contained in this dense history of the 27-year war between Athens & allies against Sparta & its allies. It breaks off near the end of the 21st year. Thucydides believed the war represented an event of unparalleled magnitude. He intended his account to serve as "a possession for all time."

raw.author: Hesiod
contexts: After bivouacking with the army in the precinct of Nemean Zeus, in which the poet Hesiod is said to have been killed by the people of the country, according to an oracle which had foretold that he should die in Nemea, Demosthenes set out at daybreak to invade Aetolia.
commentaries: Thucydides references the poet Hesiod in a brief aside about the location where his army camped, noting the tradition of his death in Nemea.

goodreads_match.description: This groundbreaking English version by Robert Fagles is the most important recent translation of Homer's great epic poem. contexts: Hellanicus, it is true, did touch on these events in his Athenian history; but he is somewhat concise and not accurate in his dates.
commentaries: The author mentions Hellanicus as a predecessor who wrote about the same events, but criticizes his conciseness and inaccuracy in dating.
